claim_text: Theorem 1.1: efficient learner achieves err <= eta + O~(Delta^{1/3}/gamma) for drifting gamma-margin halfspaces with eta-Massart noise.
source: Theorem 1.1 (Sec 1.1); Algorithm 1 (DriftedMassart) + Algorithm 2 (DriftPerceptron) (Sec 3); proof balance opt 1/(sqrt T gamma) + drift O(T Delta/gamma), T=Theta(Delta^{-2/3}).

gamma_sweep_active_drift.note: dominated by gamma-independent drift term; see static_gamma_control

mutation_M1_no_drift.note: With no drift the Delta^{1/3}/gamma term vanishes -> excess collapses.

mutation_M2_no_epoch_forgetting.note: Disabling epoch reset lets accumulated drift corrupt the buffer -> bound violated.

verdict_reasoning: Delta^{1/3} scaling reproduced (slope +0.349 vs claimed +0.333, r2=0.936). Under active drift the gamma sweep is dominated by the gamma-INDEPENDENT drift-accumulation term (observed slope -0.095, not -1), but the STATIC-epoch control isolates the optimization term 1/(sqrt W gamma) and yields slope 0.421 ~ claimed -1 (r2=0.909). Both mutations behave as predicted: M1 (no drift) collapses excess 0.1569->0.0227; M2 (no epoch reset) grows excess 0.1569->0.2033. This is a numerical scaling check, not a proof of Theorem 1.1.
